rules.text: rotli is a warm, local-first Mac menu-bar notes app — 'one brain, six fronts' (Notes · Chat · Voice · Memory · Inbox · Board). Stack: Tauri (Rust shell in src-tauri/) + React + Vite + TypeScript, Bun runtime (one bun.lock, bunfig.toml).

The user's notes are PLAIN MARKDOWN files they own, in ~/Documents/rotli/ (folders on disk = folders in the sidebar). The app's own state lives in a sibling `.rotli/` (settings · view state · index) — deletable with no data loss. The files are the source of truth; never lock notes into a proprietary store.

Low-pulse by design: no dock icon, no ⌘Tab entry, no badges/pings; summon with ⌥Space, dismiss and it's gone. Formatting/typography (Aa) is a RENDER layer — never written into the user's markdown files.

Stack discipline: Bun (one lockfile), TypeScript strict, React + Vite frontend, Tauri (Rust) shell. Dev: `bun run dev` (web) / `bun run tauri dev` (app). Run `bun run check` (and `bun run check:hex` for brand colors) before calling work done.

rotli can READ smBrain as an optional .md corpus and write back via the memex conversation contract — it OWNS chats/ (named, attachable conversations), never history/ (that's Breve's). Resolve memex roots via the contract; mirror-not-import the boundary, exactly like Breve does. See smBrain wiki/projects/rotli/smbrain-integration.

'Everything has a chat' — any object can carry a chat (chats/<slug>.md, attachedTo: [[note]]). The Convex + CRDT multi-device sync is a DESIGN (smBrain wiki/projects/rotli/sync-design), NOT yet wired — today's build is local-first, single-device (Stage 1, Phases 0–1c).

Docs live in docs/; the brand kit + brand home live in smLab (apps/rotli + brand/kits/rotli). Change code that a doc describes → update the doc (+ a CHANGELOG entry) in the same commit — see the global DOCS domain.

decisions.decision: Notes are plain markdown files the user owns in ~/Documents/rotli/; the app keeps only derived state in a sibling .rotli/ (deletable without data loss).
decisions.rationale: Local-first, no lock-in: files openable in any editor, backable-up, forever. The app is 'a warm window onto them,' not their owner.
